title: Topology-aware shadow + hybrid canary orchestration with capacity-tier negotiation
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: Current rollout primitives support simple canaries, A/B splits, and shadowing, but they do not take live topology and tiered capacity constraints into account. This gap causes either unnecessary rollbacks when regional transient capacity dips occur or unsafe rollforwards when a variant only appears compatible at API shape level but fails under production traffic characteristics (latency p99 spikes, OOM patterns, subtle tokenization drift).

Goal: Implement a topology-aware orchestration layer that coordinates hybrid rollout strategies: staged shadowing + active canary, capacity-tier negotiation, and automated rollback/escape paths. The controller should: 1) negotiate per-variant "compatibility hints" (schema, tokenizer-hash, kv-cache-consumptions, quantization-profile), 2) allocate traffic across region/capacity tiers using soft budget constraints, 3) run shadow probes in selected topology-aware cohorts before promoting traffic, and 4) synthesize policy-driven fast-fail and graceful-degrade flows to compatible variants (e.g., quantized or lower-seq-length variant) instead of blanket rollback.

Non-goals: this ticket does not build the full UI for experiment configuration (Console work will follow) and does not change billing models. It focuses on runtime controller, API surface, and telemetry used for automatic decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes new rollout API allowing: policy rules (percentage schedule, shadow cohorts by region), capacity budget targets, and compatibility-hint checks
Controller can run topology-aware shadow probes that mirror 1% of live traffic for selected variants in at least two regions without impacting host SLOs
Automated rollback triggers include a composite signal (latency p99 > baseline * 2 AND error-rate increase > 0.5%) and a separate per-customer degradation detector
Controller can failover to an explicitly compatible fallback variant (e.g., quantized v2) when region capacity is exhausted instead of global rollback
End-to-end test harness simulates cross-region capacity pressure and validates policy-prescribed graceful-degrade path
Telemetry surfaced: rollout-level timeline, per-variant cost delta, regional capacity consumption, and probe success rates
implementation_notes:
Architecture sketch: add a topo-aware scheduler component in the deployment-orchestrator that queries capacity API and variant-metadata service. Variants publish compatibility-hints during model onboarding. Scheduler computes cohort assignment with constraints solver: minimize expected latency deviation subject to regional budget. Shadow probes run with trace_id prefix and are tagged so Console can correlate. Rollback manager evaluates composite signals over sliding windows and triggers either rollback, partial-eviction (drain high-cost tier traffic), or fallback substitution. We'll reuse existing circuit-breaker and admission-control modules; extend admission-control to support soft budget enforcement.

Key data-model changes: variant metadata -> tokenizer_hash, kv_cache_estimate, seq_length_profile, quantized_alternatives, region_allowed_flags. New APIs: /rollouts/create (policy JSON), /rollouts/{id}/probe-status, /rollouts/{id}/decision. Use existing auth and audit log plumbing.

Safety: default rollout policy for new projects should keep shadowing-only for first 48 hours and require manual promotion. For P0 customers we allow shorter shadow windows via enterprise flag.
migration_steps: Schema: add compatibility fields to model-catalog and backfill for common models
Controller: implement scheduler and probe runner behind feature flag
E2E tests: add simulated capacity pressure scenarios to the infra test harness
Feature flag: enable gradual ramp to 100% orchestrator traffic for internal deployments
Docs: draft API and operator doc for rollout policy semantics
testing_plan: Unit tests for constraint solver and policy parser
Integration: deploy controller in staging with synthetic shadow traffic and assert no impact to SLOs
Chaos test: artificially starve region GPUs and verify graceful-degrade to fallback variants without global rollback
Load: verify scheduler decision latency under 10ms for fleets of 1000+ variants
Canary: run on internal org with low-traffic routes for two weeks before wider enablement
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: incorrect compatibility hints allow incompatible variant to be promoted -> mitigate with mandatory probe gate and progressive traffic caps
Risk: scheduler decisions oscillate under noisy signals -> mitigate with hysteresis windows and quorum of signals across regions
Risk: added complexity increases attack surface for security -> restrict rollout API to org-admins and require audit logs
Risk: cost blowup from shadowing -> default to small cohort sizes and conservative sampling rates
